summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Hagley Oval commenced with high tactical intensity as Bangladesh posted 289/10 (84.3 ov) in their opening innings. In response, New Zealand countered with 354/10 (92.4 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Collapse: Lost 9 Wickets for 115 Runs, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Tim Southee delivered a masterclass for New Zealand (17 Runs & 8 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (New Zealand 49%) and allowing New Zealand to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Bangladesh faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. New Zealand's bowling unit, bolstered by Shakib Hasan (67 Runs & 5 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing New Zealand won by 9 wickets in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: New Zealand's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Bangladesh produced fighting phases, New Zealand won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
